episodes.title: What Is Sociology?
episodes.description: Introduce the sociological perspective and its origins in concerns about social problems.

episodes.title: Major Sociological Paradigms
episodes.description: Compare sociology's three major theoretical frameworks and their relative strengths and limitations.

episodes.title: Sociology & the Scientific Method
episodes.description: Contrast empirical, interpretive, and critical approaches to investigating social life.

episodes.title: Sociology Research Methods
episodes.description: Follow sociological research from questions and hypotheses through data collection and analysis.

episodes.title: Émile Durkheim on Suicide & Society
episodes.description: Explore Durkheim's social facts, shared consciousness, and approach to studying social connections.

episodes.title: Karl Marx & Conflict Theory
episodes.description: Connect Marx's historical materialism and class struggles with later conflict theories and hegemony.

episodes.title: Dubois & Race Conflict
episodes.description: Explore Du Bois's work on race, double consciousness, racial formation, and social inequality.

episodes.title: Harriet Martineau & Gender Conflict Theory
episodes.description: Examine Martineau's contributions alongside feminist movements, gender conflict, and intersectionality.

episodes.title: Max Weber & Modernity
episodes.description: Explore Weber's account of rationalization, bureaucracy, legitimacy, and changes accompanying modern society.

episodes.title: Symbols, Values, & Norms
episodes.description: Investigate material and nonmaterial culture through language, symbols, values, beliefs, and social rules.

episodes.title: Cultures, Subcultures, and Countercultures
episodes.description: Compare cultural categories and use sociological theories to interpret their social significance.

episodes.title: How We Got Here
episodes.description: Classify societies through technology and compare foundational explanations of social change and solidarity.

episodes.title: Social Development
episodes.description: Explore how social interaction, care, heredity, and environment shape individual development.

episodes.title: Socialization
episodes.description: Examine socialization through families, schools, peers, media, and institutions that reshape identity.

episodes.title: Social Interaction & Performance
episodes.description: Use statuses, roles, and performance to understand everyday interaction and constructed social realities.

episodes.title: Social Groups
episodes.description: Explore group membership, leadership, conformity, networks, and the dynamics between individuals and groups.

episodes.title: Formal Organizations
episodes.description: Examine bureaucracies and how organizations respond to environments and the consequences of rationalization.

episodes.title: Deviance
episodes.description: Compare biological, psychological, and sociological explanations for behavior labeled deviant.

episodes.title: Theory & Deviance
episodes.description: Use major sociological frameworks to examine deviance's functions, meanings, and relationship with power.

episodes.title: Crime
episodes.description: Examine crime definitions and arrest statistics while considering the limitations of official data.

episodes.title: Social Stratification
episodes.description: Compare open and closed social hierarchies, including class-based and caste-based systems.

episodes.title: Why is there Social Stratification?
episodes.description: Explore explanations for hierarchy, the role of ideology, and inequality in everyday interaction.

episodes.title: Social Stratification in the US
episodes.description: Investigate the challenges of defining social class in the United States.

episodes.title: Social Class & Poverty in the US
episodes.description: Compare broad class groupings and examine the experience of poverty in American society.

episodes.title: The Impacts of Social Class
episodes.description: Connect class differences in beliefs, daily life, and health with inequality across generations.

episodes.title: Social Mobility
episodes.description: Compare forms of social mobility and examine how opportunities vary by class, race, and gender.

episodes.title: Global Stratification & Poverty
episodes.description: Examine income-based country classifications and the consequences and explanations of worldwide poverty.

episodes.title: Theories of Global Stratification
episodes.description: Contrast modernization and dependency theories, including colonial legacies and the capitalist world economy.

episodes.title: Economic Systems & the Labor Market
episodes.description: Compare economic sectors, historical transformations, capitalism, and socialism.

episodes.title: Politics
episodes.description: Explore authority, political systems, and sociological explanations of who holds power.

episodes.title: Sex & Sexuality
episodes.description: Apply sociology's major theoretical perspectives to sexuality and sexual orientations.

episodes.title: Gender Stratification
episodes.description: Explore gender socialization and its relationship with unequal educational, economic, and social outcomes.

episodes.title: Theories of Gender
episodes.description: Compare functionalist, interactionist, and conflict explanations of gender's place in society.

episodes.title: Race & Ethnicity
episodes.description: Distinguish race from ethnicity and explore how these categories change across societies and time.

episodes.title: Racial/Ethnic Prejudice & Discrimination
episodes.description: Investigate prejudice, stereotypes, institutional racism, and different forms of interaction between racial groups.

episodes.title: Age & Aging
episodes.description: Explore biological, psychological, and cultural dimensions of growing older.

episodes.title: Theories About Family & Marriage
episodes.description: Compare family forms, marriage practices, residence patterns, descent, and sociological explanations of family life.

episodes.title: Stages of Family Life
episodes.description: Explore family transitions and changing American patterns of marriage, childbearing, and household structure.

episodes.title: Religion
episodes.description: Compare interpretations of religion's sacred meanings, social cohesion, inequality, and patterns of practice.

episodes.title: Education In Society
episodes.description: Explore education's history, organization, social functions, and self-fulfilling expectations in classrooms.

episodes.title: Schools & Social Inequality
episodes.description: Use conflict theory to examine funding differences, cultural capital, and disadvantages within American schools.

episodes.title: Health & Medicine
episodes.description: Introduce medical sociology and society's influence on ideas about illness and well-being.

episodes.title: Population Health
episodes.description: Compare population health indicators and individual, environmental, and social sources of health differences.

episodes.title: The Structure & Cost of US Health Care
episodes.description: Examine American health-care access, payment arrangements, insurance, and factors that raise costs.
